q: You overtake the runner in second place. What place are you in now?
h: You take the second runner's place. The leader is still up ahead.

q: The nachos come with a bowl of green guacamole. What did the cook mash?
h: Mashed avocado gives this Mexican dip its creamy base. Lime juice is often added.

q: The prop room finds a DeLorean fitted with a time machine. Which film set wants it back?
h: Doc Brown converts the car into a time machine, and Marty takes it for a very unusual drive.

q: Turn a rectangular photo frame from portrait to landscape. What's the smallest turn that works?
h: A quarter turn puts the long edge across the top. A half turn leaves the frame in portrait.

q: You bowl down nine pins, then get the last one with your second ball. What's on the scoreboard?
h: Clear the remaining pins on the second ball of a frame and you score a spare, marked with a slash.

q: A torch and a wall stay put. Move your hand between them closer to the torch. What happens to its shadow?
h: The light spreads out from the torch. A hand nearer the light blocks a wider patch on the wall.

q: Put a prize on each corner of a chessboard. How many prizes sit on white squares?
h: An 8-by-8 board alternates colours. Opposite corners match, so two are white and two are black.

q: Three friends act out a solar eclipse as the Sun, Earth and Moon. Who stands in the middle?
o: All three in the same spot
h: The Moon passes between Earth and the Sun, hiding some or all of the Sun from view.

q: Which swimmer comes to the surface to breathe air through a blowhole?
h: A dolphin is a mammal. Its blowhole on top of its head leads to its lungs.

q: Opposite sides of a die add up to seven. If a two faces up, what number is on the table?
h: Top and bottom are opposite faces. Seven minus two leaves five.

q: Two violins and a viola arrive for a standard string quartet rehearsal. Who's missing?
h: The standard quartet has two violins, a viola and a cello. The cello plays the lowest part.

q: A holiday photo was taken at latitude 0°. Which line on a globe runs through the spot?
h: Latitude starts at the equator. The prime meridian marks zero longitude instead.

q: What gives the soaked ladyfingers in a classic tiramisu their familiar bitter aroma?
h: The sponge biscuits are dipped in coffee and layered with mascarpone cream.

q: 🎃 A glass slipper and a pumpkin carriage turn up backstage. Which fairy tale is on tonight?
h: The magic wears off at midnight and one glass slipper is left on the palace steps.

q: The starting signal sounds at an Olympic triathlon. Which event comes first?
h: Triathletes swim, switch to their bikes and finish the race on foot.

q: A red panda grips bamboo with a “false thumb”. Which body part forms it?
h: An enlarged wrist bone works with the digits of the front paw to hold a bamboo stem.

q: Round pizzas come in 20 cm and 30 cm diameters. Which order has the most surface area on top?
h: The large pizza covers 225π cm². Two small ones together cover 200π cm².

q: A box has plenty of red, blue and yellow tickets. How many blind picks guarantee two of the same colour?
h: The first three might all be different. The fourth has to match a colour you've already picked.

q: On a hot day the Eiffel Tower's iron warms evenly. Compared with a cold day, what happens to its height?
h: Iron expands as it warms. The change is small but it adds up over the height of the tower.

q: A drummer hits a drum six times, exactly one second apart. How long from the first hit to the last?
h: Six hits leave five gaps. If the first lands at zero, the sixth lands at five seconds.

q: A sound travels the same distance through room-temperature air or seawater. In which does it arrive sooner?
h: Sound travels at about 340 m/s in air and about 1,500 m/s in seawater.

q: Four quiz teams play each other exactly once. How many matches go on the schedule?
h: The first team needs three matches. The next adds two new pairings and the next adds one more.

q: Look at the black keys around the middle of a piano. What sizes of groups alternate?
h: Two black keys sit above the gaps after C and D, then three after F, G and A.

q: You film exactly three seconds of the party at 24 frames per second. How many frames can you print?
h: There are 24 separate images each second, so three seconds gives 24 × 3 = 72.

q: You're making meringue kisses. Which part of an egg do you whip with the sugar?
h: The proteins in whipped egg white trap air. Sugar helps stabilise the foam.

q: Pop! What builds up pressure inside the closed hull of a popcorn kernel as it heats?
h: Moisture inside turns to steam. The hull bursts under pressure and the starch puffs up.

q: Photo finish in the 100 metres! Which body part decides who crossed the line first?
h: The finish is judged when the torso reaches the near edge of the line. An outstretched hand doesn't count.

q: Hang six photos in a row. Use one clip at each outer end and one at each shared edge. How many clips?
h: Six photos meet at five inside edges. Add the two end clips for seven.

q: You're facing a rainbow after a shower. Where is the Sun relative to you?
o: Right in front of the lens
h: Sunlight bends and reflects inside raindrops. The rainbow appears on the opposite side of the sky from the Sun.

q: An octopus has a heart for each of its two gills. Counting the heart for the rest of its body, how many in all?
h: Two hearts pump blood to the gills. A third pumps oxygenated blood around the body.

q: You write one ticket each for numbers 1 through 20. How many times do you write the digit 1?
h: The tens place contributes ten from 10 through 19. The ones place adds two, in 1 and 11.

q: Which planet takes longer to spin once on its axis than to make a full trip around the Sun?
h: One rotation of Venus takes about 243 Earth days. One orbit takes only about 225.

q: A prize costs 100 points. Take 20% off, then add 20% of the reduced price. What's the final price?
h: The discount is 20 points, but the increase is 20% of 80, just 16 points. That gives 96.

q: Paint all six sides of a cube gold, then cut it into 3×3×3 equal cubes. How many have exactly two gold faces?
h: Only the middle cube on each edge has two painted faces. A cube has twelve edges.

q: One box holds the prize. Exactly one clue is true: “not A”, “in B”, “not B”. Which box wins?
h: Exactly one of the two B clues must be true. So “not A” must be false, putting the prize in A.

q: Sixteen teams enter a single-elimination bracket with no third-place match. How many matches produce one winner?
h: Each match eliminates one team. Fifteen teams must leave before there's just one winner.

q: Two fair six-sided dice roll independently. Which of these totals is most likely?
h: Seven has six ordered combinations, from (1,6) to (6,1). Two has one, five has four and ten has three.

q: It's exactly 3:30 on a clock with continuously moving hands. What's the smaller angle between them?
h: The minute hand points at 6. The hour hand is halfway from 3 to 4, leaving 2½ hour marks at 30° each.

q: Which film became the first non-English-language Best Picture winner at the 2020 Oscars?
h: Bong Joon Ho's film won Best Picture, Directing, Original Screenplay and International Feature Film.

q: A stage screen sets a pixel's red, green and blue channels all to maximum. What colour does it display?
h: RGB screens add light. Turning all three channels fully on produces white.

q: Two stage lights just flashed together. One flashes every 6 seconds, the other every 8. When do they next coincide?
h: The first shared multiple of six and eight is 24. That's four cycles of one light and three of the other.

q: Stir a spoonful of coffee into tea, then spoon the same volume back. Which drink lost more to the other cup?
o: It depends on the starting volumes
h: Each cup returns to its original volume. The missing coffee in its cup is replaced by exactly that volume of tea.

q: Greenland can look as big as Africa on a Mercator map. Where does this projection exaggerate area most?
h: Scale increases towards high latitudes, so Greenland looks much larger relative to Africa than it really is.

q: Where do flamingos get most of the pigments that give their feathers that pink glow?
h: Algae and small crustaceans supply carotenoid pigments, which contribute to the colour of a flamingo's feathers.

q: One bag is red, one blue, one mixed. Every label is wrong. Which labelled bag lets one draw identify all three?
h: The bag marked “mixed” has only one colour. Knowing which one leaves only one way to correct the other two labels.
